item.title: Kava Bill 2026 is not law yet, public will get another chance to have their say - Rabuka
item.description: Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says the Kava Bill 2026 is not yet law and Fijians will have another chance to have their say before it is passed. Rabuka made the clarification following public concerns over the Bill’s proposed registration requirements and penalties, and criticism that the Coalition Government has lost touch with ordinary Fijians.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says the Kava Bill 2026 is not yet law and Fijians will have another chance to have their say before it is passed.

Rabuka made the clarification following public concerns over the Bill’s proposed registration requirements and penalties, and criticism that the Coalition Government has lost touch with ordinary Fijians.

He says the Bill has been introduced in Parliament and will be referred by the Speaker to the relevant Parliamentary Committee.

Rabuka says the Committee will conduct its own public consultations, hear submissions from people across the country and has the power to recommend changes to the proposed legislation.

He says those who have concerns about the Bill in its current form should make their views known during the Parliamentary Committee consultations.

The Prime Minister says after the Committee presents its report, the Bill will proceed to its third reading, where it will be debated before Parliament decides whether it should be passed.

Rabuka says the development of laws in Fiji involves consultation with the public, and concerns raised by people are considered when legislation is drafted.

He says the Kava Bill was developed following consultations with people involved in the industry, particularly on measures they believe are needed to protect the sector and prevent exploitation.

Rabuka says democracy requires consultation and laws should ultimately reflect what the majority of the country wants for an important industry such as kava.

He says the Government remains committed to transparent and inclusive law-making that puts the interests of ordinary Fijians at the centre of the legislative process.

item.title: Special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum on Online Safety to be held at 7pm Friday September 4th
item.description: A special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan will go live at 7pm Friday September 4th. The theme of the forum is Online Safety: Connected and Protected?
item.content:encoded:
A special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan will go live at 7pm Friday September 4th.

The theme of the forum is Online Safety: Connected and Protected?

The panelists for the public forum will be Online Safety Commissioner, Filipe Batiwale, Fiji Law Reform Commissioners David Solvalu and Valerie Narain.

The Straight Talk forum will focus on Online Safety Issues in Fiji, what is being faced by the Online Safety Commission, the feedback from the members of the public during the consultation process on the review of the Online Safety Act 2018, the call for age restrictions for Social Media, the response from victims, the changes being proposed and the reasons behind them amongst other issues.

You can also be part of the live audience by applying for registration with a question that you would like to ask during the forum.

The application to register details can be found on our website and facebook page, fijivillage.

You will receive a confirmation if you have been selected to be part of the live audience.

Please apply early to avoid any disappointment.

The show will be broadcast live at 7pm Friday September 4th on our Facebook, YouTube and X.

item.title: PM says we will have elections by Feb 6th 2027 under existing laws if constitution review is not over
item.description: Karishma Kumari , Vijay Narayan · 02/09/2026 Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says the Constitution Review Commission report should be made public, and will be released after Cabinet meets. While this process is being undertaken, Rabuka stresses that we must have the elections by February 6th 2027 and if things are not ready, then the elections will be held under the existing laws and regulat
item.content:encoded:
Karishma Kumari , Vijay Narayan · 02/09/2026

Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says the Constitution Review Commission report should be made public, and will be released after Cabinet meets. While this process is being undertaken, Rabuka stresses that we must have the elections by February 6th 2027 and if things are not ready, then the elections will be held under the existing laws and regulations.

Rabuka says an electronic version of the review report will also be available and will probably be posted for people to look at rather than having to access the voluminous physical document. When questioned on whether Government intends to select certain recommendations from the report rather than present it in its entirety, Rabuka says they will not be picking certain parts. He says most of the report will be presented to the public and to the committee that will consider it, before it is debated in Parliament as a whole. When asked whether the next general elections would still be held under the current Constitution if the constitutional review process proceeds, Rabuka says this will depend on how much progress has been made or they would have done before the elections timeline which is by February 6th 2027.

item.title: Richard Naidu challenges FICAC evidence as hearsay in Prof. Prasad trial
item.description: Former Deputy Prime Minister Professor Biman Prasad's lawyer Richard Naidu says FICAC is twisting and turning in its attempts to have a disputed document admitted as evidence in the trial. The disputed document relates to Platinum Hotels and Resorts PTE Limited and contains details of the company's directors and secretary.
item.content:encoded:
Former Deputy Prime Minister Professor Biman Prasad's lawyer Richard Naidu says FICAC is twisting and turning in its attempts to have a disputed document admitted as evidence in the trial.

The disputed document relates to Platinum Hotels and Resorts PTE Limited and contains details of the company's directors and secretary.

Naidu argues that the document is hearsay and that the person who prepared it must give evidence.

He says they do not even know who prepared the document and its contents must be proven to be true.

Naidu says a hearsay document is not admissible and does not constitute the best evidence.

Meanwhile, FICAC lawyer Joseph Work says the document is not hearsay as it qualifies as a public document.

Work says the evidence does not fall under the criteria of hearsay because of the statutory nature of the document and has asked for the objection to be dismissed.

Magistrate Prasad will make his ruling at 11.30am this Friday.

Professor Prasad is charged with failure to comply with statutory disclosure requirements contrary to section 24 (5) of the Political Parties Act.

FICAC alleges that between 30th December 2015 to 31st January 2016, in Suva, being an officeholder of the National Federation Party, registered under the Political Parties (Registration, Conduct, Funding and Disclosures) Act 2013, failed to comply with Section 24(1B)(d), by providing to the office of the registrar his declaration of assets, liabilities and income as at 31st December 2015 without disclosing his directorship in Platinum Hotels & Resorts PTE Limited thereby committing an offence contrary to section 24(5) of the said Act.

It is also alleged that on 28th January 2016 in Suva, being an office holder of a registered political party, namely the National Federation Party, recklessly provided false information in a statutory declaration submitted to the Registrar of Political Parties under Section 24 (1B) (d) of the Political Parties (Registration, Conduct, Funding and Disclosures) Act 2013, solemnly declaring that the particular contained in his declaration of assets, liabilities and income as at 31st December 2015 were true and complete when the declaration omitted his directorship in Platinum Hotels and Resorts PTE Limited, which omission rendered the declaration false in material particular thereby committing an offence contrary to Section 27 (1) (c) of the said Act.

item.title: Rabuka confirms approaching Justice Ashton-Lewis for CJ's role, says friendship now rules him out
item.description: Karishma Kumari , Vijay Narayan · 02/09/2026 Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka has today confirmed that he had approached Justice David Ashton-Lewis before and after the 2022 general elections and had asked Justice Ashton-Lewis if he was interested in becoming the Chief Justice of Fiji.
item.content:encoded:
Karishma Kumari , Vijay Narayan · 02/09/2026

Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka has today confirmed that he had approached Justice David Ashton-Lewis before and after the 2022 general elections and had asked Justice Ashton-Lewis if he was interested in becoming the Chief Justice of Fiji.

Rabuka also confirms that they had been looking for a suitable candidate for the position but stresses that any appointment would have to go through the normal selection process.

He says the matter does not rest with Cabinet and involves the Judicial Services Commission, the Attorney-General and the Prime Minister.

When asked whether he still had plans to appoint Justice Ashton-Lewis as Chief Justice of Fiji, Rabuka says he cannot be considered for the position due to a conflict of interest, as they are both friends.

When questioned by fijivillage News about asking Justice Ashton-Lewis and Janet Mason to identify the "crocodiles in the pond" during the Commission of Inquiry into the appointment of Barbara Malimali as FICAC Commissioner, referring to people believed to be undermining his Prime Ministership, Rabuka said he made these comments in view of the specific subject of the Commission of Inquiry, which was the selection or appointment of Barbara Malimali.

He says there were some words of those who were trying to support her into that and for something that she could do for them afterwards .

Rabuka says he was trying to establish whether there were people supporting Malimali's appointment because they expected something in return.

Following comments about Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica being regarded as one of the "crocodiles in the pond", Rabuka says he did not believe this simply on the basis of association, adding that the Minister was a friend of a group of people and he did not want any of his Cabinet Ministers involved or suspected of being involved.

Meanwhile, in an interview on fijivillage Straight Talk With Vijay Narayan, Justice Ashton Lewis confirmed that Rabuka had spoken to him before and after the 2022 general elections and had asked Ashton-Lewis whether he was interested in becoming the Chief Justice of Fiji.

Justice Ashton Lewis also confirms that Rabuka had asked him and Janet Mason to identify the crocodiles in the pond before the COI and said that they had identified Deputy Prime Minister, Manoa Kamikamica was identified as one of the crocodiles in the pond.

The Suva Magistrates Court has ruled there was no case to answer for Kamikamica after he was charged by FICAC for perjury during the Commission of Inquiry proceedings.

item.title: At least 1,200 dead, more than 4,200 missing after Nepal floods
item.description: At least 1,200 people have died and more than 4,200 remain missing in Nepal as rescue and relief operations intensify a week after catastrophic flash floods struck along the Nepal-Tibet border. Nepal’s disaster agency says nearly 12,000 people have been rescued , while efforts are continuing to reach workers, potentially in the hundreds, believed to be trapped inside hydropower tunnels.
item.content:encoded:
At least 1,200 people have died and more than 4,200 remain missing in Nepal as rescue and relief operations intensify a week after catastrophic flash floods struck along the Nepal-Tibet border.

Nepal’s disaster agency says nearly 12,000 people have been rescued , while efforts are continuing to reach workers, potentially in the hundreds, believed to be trapped inside hydropower tunnels.

On the Tibetan side of the border, Chinese state media says 21 people have died and more than 540 remain unaccounted for.

The massive flash flood, believed to have been triggered by a glacial collapse last Wednesday, swept through a Himalayan valley and destroyed villages.

More than 40 bridges have been destroyed, making access to some of the worst-hit areas difficult.

Chinese and Indian experts are helping construct temporary bridges to reach remote areas, while drones are being used to search areas that rescuers cannot easily access.

Some remote communities are relying on army helicopters for essential supplies, while villages continue to face shortages of fuel and electricity.

In Nepal, nearly 3,500 people have been left homeless and displaced across 27 sites, mostly schools, in the Nuwakot and Rasuwa districts.

The United Nations says the priority is now delivering aid, recovering those who died, tracing missing relatives and reuniting separated children.

The UN has warned that overcrowded shelters, contaminated water and damaged health facilities are increasing the risk of disease during the monsoon season.

Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah says there is now a renewed focus on protecting survivors and providing medical treatment and psychological counselling.

Shah says the disaster was beyond predictable forecasts but acknowledged the growing risks facing the Himalayan region because of climate change.

Nepal has declared a disaster in 15 affected areas for three months to provide financial assistance to families, relocate displaced people and deploy the army.

The Nepalese Government and the UN have also agreed to launch a four-month humanitarian appeal.

item.title: 2-yr-old Rajveer wins first place at Hibiscus Baby Show
item.description: Two-year-old Rajveer Chand won first place in Category 4 of the Hibiscus Baby Show held at the Suva Civic Centre today. A last-minute decision to enter her firstborn in the show ended in a proud moment for Sanjeshni Sangeeta Kumar and her family.
item.content:encoded:
Two-year-old Rajveer Chand won first place in Category 4 of the Hibiscus Baby Show held at the Suva Civic Centre today.

A last-minute decision to enter her firstborn in the show ended in a proud moment for Sanjeshni Sangeeta Kumar and her family.

Chand won first place in Category 4, which was open to children aged between one and three years.

Kumar, who lives in Nadawa, says she only saw an advertisement for the Baby Show on facebook yesterday before deciding to give it a try.

She says she and her husband decided to bring Rajveer along, little knowing that he would return home as a winner.

She says her aunt would often win, making her an inspiration and encouraging her to take part with her own children.

Kumar says the win was particularly special for her family as Rajveer was born after seven years of marriage and is a much-loved and cherished child.

Kumar is now a mother of two, with her second child only two weeks old.

She says her husband has also played an important role in caring for Rajveer, particularly after she underwent Caesarean sections for both of her children .

Insert: Kumar - All the credit goes to him Sept 02
